red_interpretation: The two red vertical lines are the stitch lines of two vertical waist-suppression darts sewn into the back body panel — fish-shaped stitched seams that pinch out fabric for a trimmer waist. They are construction seams only: not pleats, not contrast fabric, not decorative lines. There are no red marks at the yoke seam, so the yoke join is plain and smooth with zero pleats.
geometry_summary: Rear view, long-sleeve dress shirt. Standard straight horizontal back yoke with a single dashed stitch row at its lower seam (yoke seam at ~30% of drawn body height, y=44/191). One-piece back panel below the yoke — completely smooth at the yoke join, no folds, no center-back line. Two straight, vertical, parallel red dart lines placed symmetrically about center-back: left dart x=69-70, right dart x=117-119, center-back x=94, body side seams x=45/146 (waist width ~100px). Each dart is drawn as a single line and runs from y=80 to y=163 — i.e., the dart apex starts ~25% below the yoke seam (just below the armhole / shoulder-blade level) and the dart terminates ~84% down the body, at high-hip level, stopping well short of the hem. Curved shirttail hem with dashed hem stitching; sleeves with plackets and buttoned cuffs are peripheral, not the feature.
counts: Pleats: 0. Darts: 2 (one left of center-back, one right, symmetric). Dart stitch lines: 1 per dart as drawn. Yoke seams: 1 horizontal yoke seam (single dashed stitch row as drawn). Other seams: 2 side seams, 2 armhole seams, 1 hemmed shirttail. No center-back seam or pleat.
locked_features: Exactly two vertical darts, no more, no fewer, placed symmetrically left and right of center-back
Each dart begins below the shoulder blade (about a quarter of the way down the body from the yoke seam) and ends at high-hip level, clearly stopping above the hem
Darts are straight, vertical, and parallel, rendered as real stitched dart seams with fabric suppression that shapes the waist inward
Plain straight horizontal yoke with a smooth, flat yoke-to-body join: zero pleats and zero gathering anywhere along the yoke seam
Center back is completely plain: no box pleat, no center crease, no center seam from yoke to hem
One-piece back panel with curved shirttail hem; darts do not reach the hem
ratios: Each dart sits approximately midway between center-back and the side seam (dart offset ~48% of the half-width from center-back)
Dart-to-dart spacing ~48% of the full back width at the waist (~18-20 cm on a real shirt)
Dart top starts ~25% of the yoke-to-hem length below the yoke seam
Dart bottom ends ~84% down the yoke-to-hem length, leaving ~16% of body length dart-free above the hem
Dart length ~58% of the yoke-to-hem body length (~30-34 cm real-world)
Yoke depth ~30% of total drawn back height; body below yoke ~70%
uncertain: Dart suppression amount (fabric take-up at the widest point, typically 1-1.5 cm per dart) is not specified by the drawing — each dart is drawn as a single uniform line with no width or taper profile
Whether the yoke seam carries one or two rows of topstitching — the drawing shows a single dashed row, but line weight at this resolution cannot rule out a twin-needle finish
Exact hem depth and hem stitch style are drawn only as a generic dashed line
